evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Donau: Abnobius, Danubius
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the name of the upper river; the lower course was called Ister. Lewis & Short calls the spelling Danubius a late corruption.
Also spelled Ister, less correctly (Lewis & Short); the poets use both names for the whole river.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
